newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco Sudbury union seeks mediator in talks.
newsitem.headline: Inco Sudbury union seeks mediator in talks.

text.p: The union representing 4700 Inco Ltd employees said on Monday it has requested the assistance of a provincial mediator in contracts talks with the Canadian nickel giant.

"Nickel and copper prices are high, market conditions are great for both the short and long term, and the union is demanding a fair share for its members," Wayne Fraser, chair of the United Steelworkers' negotiating team, said in a statement.
The current contract expires at midnight, Saturday, May 31. The last time the union requested mediation was in 1982.
Fraser said contract talks reached an impasse on Saturday.
Workers at Inco's Ontario operations have voted 98 percent in favor of giving union leaders a mandate to strike if a tentative agreement cannot be reached by May 31.
The contract affects 4,700 workers at the nickel giant's mining, smelting and refinery operations in Sudbury and its refinery in Port Colborne.
